messages.author: c40bbc4593a08753
messages.subject: DIANN-MSstats groupComparison Issue
parts:
Dear MSstats team,

I have encountered an error when I am analysing DIANN protein-level DIA data in MSstats. I am able to carry out the conversion and data summarisation fine. But when I carry out the group comparison function, it finishes the calculations but then gives an error regarding 'undefined columns selected' (see below). The full data is quite large so I have cut it and this has given me the same error (see below). I have attached the files here.

model.no <- groupComparison(contrast.matrix = comparison, data=quant.no, use_log_file = FALSE)
INFO  [2023-11-28 12:42:27]  == Start to test and get inference in whole plot ...
  |===============================================================================================================| 100%
INFO  [2023-11-28 12:42:28]  == Comparisons for all proteins are done.
Error in `[.data.frame`(as.data.frame(comparisons), , cols) :
  undefined columns selected

This indicates that there's probably something wrong with my 'comparison' matrix. So, I then tried to use MSstatsShiny, but this gave a similar message (see attached).

Has anyone seen this issue before?

On a separate note, I am finding that the Protein Level data groups are different from the Feature Level data groups (see below). Do you know what could cause this? This also happens with Proteome Discoverer data too. I have to manually change it in R.
> unique(quant.no$ProteinLevelData$GROUP)
[1] 10 ng  50 ng  200 ng 20 ng  5 ng  
Levels: 5 ng 10 ng 20 ng 50 ng 200 ng
> unique(quant.no$FeatureLevelData$GROUP)
[1] 4 5 2 3 1
Levels: 1 2 3 4 5

I am using MSstats v4.10.0, MSConvert v1.12

Many thanks,
Amandeep

messages.author: 13904eb0f06097b0
messages.subject: Re: DIANN-MSstats groupComparison Issue
parts:
Hi Amandeep, 

Sorry for the delay, this was a weird problem to solve. The problem is due to the lme4 package which we use to fit some statistical models in the groupComparison function. It has an issue with the older versions of the library Matrix that are not solved automatically on regular MSstats install. I was able to fix it by simply reinstalling lme4 from source:

install.packages("lme4", type = "source")

Let me know if this does not work. There is more information about this issue here:

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/77481539/error-in-initializeptr-function-cholmod-factor-ldeta-not-provided-by-pack

Best,
Devon
